topics.title: Core Concepts
topics.description: DevOps is a set of practices that combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops) to shorten the systems development life cycle while delivering features, fixes and updates frequently, reliably, and in close alignment with business objectives.

key_principles.title: Collaboration
key_principles.description: Breaking down silos between development and operations teams.

key_principles.title: Automation
key_principles.description: Automating repetitive tasks to improve efficiency.

key_principles.title: Continuous Integration and Delivery
key_principles.description: Frequently integrating code changes and delivering them to production.

key_principles.title: Monitoring
key_principles.description: Continuous monitoring of applications and infrastructure.

topics.title: CI/CD Pipeline
topics.description: Continuous integration is a development practice where developers integrate code into a shared repository frequently, preferably several times a day. Each integration is verified by an automated build and automated tests.

delivery_vs_deployment.description: The practice of automatically preparing code changes for release to production, ensuring code can be deployed at any time.
The practice of automatically deploying code changes to production after passing all tests.

pipeline_stages.title: 3. Test
pipeline_stages.description: Run unit, integration and functional tests.

pipeline_stages.title: 4. Deploy
pipeline_stages.description: Deploy to staging or production environments.

topics.description: Git is a distributed version control system that lets multiple developers collaborate by managing different versions of the codebase. The strategy you pick shapes how CI/CD, reviews and hotfixes work.

strategies.description: Simplified workflow with feature branches and a single main branch.
branches: A single main branch represents deployable code

strategies.description: Short-lived feature branches with frequent merges to trunk.
branches: Main development happens on trunk (the main branch)
Short-lived feature branches, typically under a day

topics.description: IaC is the practice of managing and provisioning infrastructure through code instead of manual processes. Configuration management sits alongside it, keeping systems in a desired, consistent state.

topics.title: Deployment Patterns
topics.description: The three release strategies used for microservices, and the process behind each.

blue_green_deployment.description: Reduces downtime by running two identical production environments.
process: Blue environment is live, green is staging
Deploy the new version to green
Switch traffic from blue to green
Blue becomes standby for the next deployment

canary_deployment.description: Gradually shifts traffic from the old version to the new one.
process: Deploy the new version alongside the old version
Route a small percentage of traffic to the new version
Gradually increase traffic to the new version

rolling_deployment.description: Updates instances of an application incrementally rather than all at once.
process: Deploy the new version to a subset of instances
Repeat until all instances are updated

questions.question: What is the difference between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
answer: CI: automating the integration of code changes
CD (Delivery): ensuring code can be deployed at any time
CD (Deployment): automatically deploying all changes to production

questions.question: How would you monitor a Spring Boot application in production?
